value.answer: A few things that help most kids: a dark, quiet room, the same short wind-down every time (a book, a song, a diaper change), and putting him down drowsy but still awake so he learns to drift off on his own. Watch for tired cues like rubbing eyes or fussing, because an overtired kid often fights sleep harder. How old is he? The timing and length of naps change a lot by age.
